title: The loudest sound in the ocean, solved

lines.text: In 1997, underwater microphones picked up a sound so loud, it was heard over 5,000 kilometres away.
It was recorded by a hydrophone array run by NOAA, in the Pacific Ocean.
It was far more powerful than any known animal call.
So people started wondering. Was something enormous living down there?
For years, it fuelled theories about unknown sea monsters.
The real answer turned out to be ice.
The sound matched an icequake, a huge piece of glacier cracking and breaking away.
Still, it's a reminder. The ocean is louder, and stranger, than we think.

sources.claim: Recorded 1997 by NOAA's Equatorial Pacific hydrophone array; detected over 5,000 km; far more powerful than any animal call; explained as a large icequake
